neighbours.label: a floating quantifier ('both', 'all', 'all of which') referring back to an already-named pair or group
fire: My brother and sister have both moved to Chicago for work.
The two reports, both written in 2019, reach the same conclusion.
She bought a lamp and a rug, both from the same flea market.
The twins were both born just after midnight in March.
Three bridges cross the river here, all built by the same engineer.
He wrote two novels last year, both about life at sea.
The tomatoes and peppers, all of which come from our garden, went into the sauce.
Our parents are both retired teachers living in Ohio.
